summary: Discovery with Silverline about sudden token surges ("token flood") on their edge inference layer. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with strict p95 SLAs during 1-3 minute bursts; they want benchmarking, fallback strategies, and security docs. AE+SE outlined Redwood batching, smart routing, and observability. Agreed next steps: share benchmark template and run Dedicated baseline.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-11-28 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Silverline Head of Platform), Ellen Park (ML Eng Lead), Samir Patel (CTO)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros — I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood inference team, and Priya here is our SE who focuses on latency and streaming.
[00:12] Marco: Hi all, Marco here. We run Silverline's inference mesh, mostly for on-device personalization and cloud sidefa — sidecar routing. Ellen and Samir are with me.
[00:22] Ellen: Hi, Ellen. We do a lot of short real-time generations and occasional long-format responses for diagnostics.
[00:29] Samir: Samir — CTO. Main thing for us is we see these token surges when feature flags roll out, and it can blow past our typical capacity.
[00:38] Priya: Thanks. So the goal for today is to map your burst profile, p95 targets, and figure out whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private is the right fit and what a pilot looks like.
[00:48] Marco: Exactly. Our p95 target varies by endpoint but generally we need p95 < 200ms for short streaming responses and p95 < 1.2s for full doc-gen flows. During bursts we spike to ~50–80k tokens/sec across region, but that can be concentrated into a 30–90s window.
[01:12] Jordan: Good, that's helpful. When you say tokens/sec — is that aggregated across all instances or per-node?
[01:18] Marco: Aggregated. Per-node during bursts is around 6–10k tokens/sec depending on model size.
[01:24] Priya: Okay. A few quick clarifying questions: what models are you serving (open/closed), average sequence length, and are you using streaming output?
[01:34] Ellen: We mostly use a 3B open model for short responses and 13B for diagnostics, with avg seq len ~40 for short and ~800 for diagnostics. Streaming for the short ones, full non-stream for long.
[01:46] Priya: That split matters — streaming has different tail behavior because of chunking and the KV cache hits for prefixes. Also can you share whether you enforce sticky sessions (to keep KV cache warm) or are requests load-balanced round robin?
[01:58] Marco: We currently do simple LB without session stickiness. Probably part of the issue.
[02:03] Samir: We're also bound by data residency — some customers require EU-only processing, which matters for Hosted.
[02:09] Jordan: Understood. For Hosted we have region-level tenancy and can route to EU, but Dedicated or Private gives you explicit isolation and often easier compliance.
[02:20] Ellen: Cost is also a factor — we want predictable unit cost during steady state, but willing to pay more for short bursts if we can guarantee p95 SLA.
[02:29] Priya: Right — typical patterns we've seen: use Hosted for general traffic, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable steady-state and use autoscale/burst capacity for short spikes, or Private for strict compliance and full control of autoscale.
[02:42] Marco: Can you give us a concrete token/sec baseline for 13B on your Dedicated nodes? Like what's p95 at 6k tokens/sec vs 10k?
[02:52] Priya: Ballpark numbers: on a tuned Dedicated 13B profile with quantization and continuous batching, at ~6k tokens/sec per node you're usually sub-500ms p95 for streaming short outputs; as you approach 10k tokens/sec you start to see p95 climb — sometimes to 700–900ms depending on request shape and batching effectiveness. Those numbers depend on kernel choice, sequence length and batching windows.
[03:19] Ellen: That helps. What about prefix/KV cache warmup — we see big tail spikes when the cache is cold.
[03:26] Priya: That's expected. We recommend warm-start strategies: session stickiness for high-traffic users, pre-populating KV for common prefixes, and a smart routing policy that favors warmed replicas during burst windows. Also Redwood Optimize can suggest cache/quantization profiles per endpoint.
[03:41] Marco: For our token-flood scenario, is a fallback to smaller model acceptable? We worry about quality regression.
[03:48] Jordan: That's a common tradeoff — fallback to a smaller model or to an abridged output format. Redwood supports automatic fallback policies by latency/capacity thresholds, and you can tie those to quality monitors so we alert on degradation.
[04:02] Samir: Security questions — can we run Private in our VPC with customer-managed KMS? And audit logs for every token stream?
[04:10] Jordan: Yes to both: Private supports customer VPCs and HSM/KMS integrations; we also capture extensive audit logs and token-level tracing in the Redwood Console. We'll share SOC2 and our KMS integration docs.
[04:21] Ellen: Great. For benchmarking, do you have a template for simulating minute-long floods with varying seq lengths?
[04:28] Priya: We do — it's a Jupyter + Locust-based harness that can simulate ramp, plateau, and decay windows for token/sec, and also generate streaming vs non-stream traffic. We'll share that.
[04:38] Marco: When you run the Dedicated baseline, what telemetry will you collect? We need p95, p99, token/sec, GPU utilization, cache hit rate, and trunked queue lengths.
[04:50] Priya: We'll collect all that and map it to Redwood metrics: per-route p95/p99, token throughput, kernel utilization, batching efficiency, kv_cache_hit_rate, and queue_latency. We'll also produce an annotated spreadsheet with recommendations.
[05:03] Jordan: Timeline wise — if we can get your traffic histogram and sample payloads by Friday, we can provision a Dedicated baseline next week and share results within 5 business days.
[05:13] Marco: That works. A couple of other notes — our infra uses Envoy sidecars and we sometimes see head-of-line blocking when many streams open at once. Anything to mitigate that?
[05:24] Priya: Head-of-line is often an application pattern. We recommend connection pooling, prioritizing open streams, and in the Redwood runtime we do continuous batching so we don't queue requests at the process level for long; plus you can configure burst concurrency caps to prevent overload.
[05:40] Ellen: Curious about quantization tradeoffs: can we run 13B quantized in Dedicated without harming diagnostic quality too much?
[05:48] Priya: In many cases 4-bit quant works for diagnostics with small drops; for very sensitive scoring we keep a float path. Redwood Optimize will give per-endpoint recommendations based on your eval sets.
[05:59] Marco: Any gotchas around streaming and GPU memory when seq len spikes to 800+?
[06:05] Priya: Long sequences increase KV cache and memory pressure; we recommend mixing dedicated nodes for long-form (higher mem profiles) and lower-latency nodes for short streaming. Also guardrail the max concurrent long-form requests.
[06:18] Samir: Ok. So next steps: baseline run, security pack, and pricing. Also want to evaluate a canary fallback that routes to smaller model under spot overload.
[06:27] Jordan: Yep. We'll send the benchmark harness, pricing, and security docs. Priya will own the baseline run and instrument the metrics.
[06:35] Marco: Quick last question — how do you handle cross-region failover during bursts? We can't cross-region for EU customers due to residency but for global customers what do you recommend?
[06:45] Priya: For global customers, smart routing can failover to other regions or to lower-cost model variants. For the EU-only flows you'd pin to EU Dedicated or Private. For global you can have a primary region and warm capacity in a secondary region with async warming.
[06:58] Ellen: Thanks. This was really helpful, gives us a clear plan.
[07:03] Jordan: Great. Recap and I'll close — 1) Marco sends histograms and sample payloads, 2) Priya runs Dedicated baseline with waveform token-flood profile week of Dec 4, 3) Jordan sends security pack and pricing, 4) follow-up meeting to review findings. Thanks all.
[07:25] (end)
notes: Customer emphasizes token surge windows (30-90s) and strict p95 goals for streaming (<200ms)
Suggested warm-start strategies and Dedicated baseline; priority on KV cache hit optimization
